purpose: Post-#652 requalification of gate-mixed-source-compose on the R640AI deployment (container knowledgevault, image built from branch zcode/652-thinking-client-timeout-streaming @ f438e010, deployed 2026-09-21 with default request timeouts 300/300/120 s). The #229 F3 cleanup had removed the original qualification drafts (post-cleanup-inventory.txt: drafts=2), so the gate was recreated end to end: fresh mixed-source compose draft (manuscript + reference, the same synthetic inputs as requa3_drafts.py) in vault 2, bench superadmin f3bench652 (deleted after the run).

deployment_config.request_timeouts: settings defaults (THINKING/EDITORIAL 300.0, INSTANT 120.0) — proving the streaming fix, not a raised budget
deviations: DRAFT_ROOM_ENABLED was flipped true for the qualification window and restored to false afterwards (.env backup restored; verified).
INGESTION_JOB_LEASE_ENABLED was flipped false mid-run while diagnosing an unrelated parse stall (see anomaly note) and restored to true afterwards.

DRAFT_EDITORIAL_CHAT_URL/MODEL were moved to the local minicpm5-2b endpoint after the two configured editorial backends failed the copy stage (see attempts 2-3); restored afterwards. This is the same class of documented environment deviation as the F3 CORS workaround.

anomaly_note: On the first boot of the fix image, the first two draft input parse jobs (jobs 32/33) ran to their 300 s draft_parse_timeout and failed job_timeout while stage extraction itself completed instantly in a separate in-container process. The condition did not reproduce on any subsequent boot across three images (pre-#650 edd2c741, master-at-fork 26cb27d6, and the fix image itself, each parsing a fresh input in <=30 s with the same config). Treated as a transient boot-window stall, not attributable to any specific commit; recorded here because it consumed the initial parse attempts for draft 9 (retried cleanly as jobs 37/38).

attempts.reading: All thinking-stage calls streamed past the old 300 s cliff (research call 1 ran ~50 min in one streamed request, outline/draft ~2-4 min each) — the #652 defect (hardcoded read timeout killing long generations) is gone. The copy stage on the configured editorial backend (192.168.1.145) exhausted its transient ladder: that server sustained 15-30 min streams but dropped them before completion (server-side close observed on the socket).
Same editorial-server stream dropping; stage cache resumed at copy exactly as designed.

Editorial endpoint temporarily pointed at the thinking vLLM (ChatGPTN): streams completed but the big-prompt CopyReport failed Pydantic validation twice ('stage copy returned invalid structured output twice'). Reverted.

verdict: pass — a mixed-source compose draft completed the full nine-stage journey (intake, research, outline, draft, lint, copy, standards, fact, assemble) against the deployed thinking server with the streaming fix live, well inside DRAFT_JOB_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=7200 (final attempt 17.0 min; the 70.8 min first attempt also stayed inside the budget and cleared every thinking-stage call past the former 300 s read-timeout cliff). Revision carries 59 citations, fact_status passed, export 200. Remaining editorial-backend fragility (192.168.1.145 stream drops) is an environment condition of that third-party server, not an application defect; the editorial endpoint is operator-configurable and was switched locally for the run with the deviation recorded above.
